name: Rosetta Stone: granodiorite and pink vein

font.display: Georgia, 'Iowan Old Style', 'Palatino Linotype', Palatino, 'Times New Roman', serif

brandSources.note: An object has no brand. The British Museum record describes the stela as 'grey and pink granodiorite'; a dark slate canvas evokes the stone's grey body once the wax and chalk were removed. Chosen by judgement, not extracted from any site.

brandSources.from: same BM record ('pink' granodiorite); the pink vein across the top left corner is mentioned in the Wikipedia article on the 1999 cleaning
brandSources.note: A soft pink picks up the stone's vein. Contrast on bg is well above 3:1. Not the British Museum's own brand colour; the page does not imitate the museum.
Gold for the decree (royal/temple gilding), cool greys and blues for loss and capture, green for decipherment, lilac for the modern debate. All kept at least 3:1 on the dark background.
Georgia-style serif for the wordmark (carved-inscription feel), system sans for body. No webfont, so the page works offline.
